# Onda for Mac — beta 120
## Guided audio-access recovery
- Onda now checks whether Spotify audio is actually reaching its room-speaker mixer, rather than treating a connected speaker or a successful audio-tap start as proof of playback. - If local music produces no captured signal for twelve seconds, a **Fix audio access** notice explains what to check. Silence can have other causes too; the app does not claim a definitive permission denial. - The guide covers audio-only permission, the stale approval that can follow a signing change, and macOS’s Quit & Reopen step. **Reconnect audio** rebuilds music sharing while keeping your speaker settings. - System Settings opens only when you choose it. Recovery actions are blocked during calls, video, microphone use and tuning; there is no automatic permission reset or app restart. - Missing Accessibility access now shows **Call access needed**, with an enable button in Settings.
Speaker levels, output assignments, saved timing and room tuning are retained. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi room-speaker paths both have the signal check. No microphone access or recordings are added for music checks.
## Updating
Existing installations with automatic updates enabled can download this release automatically; installation occurs when Onda quits. Use **Settings → Check for Updates** to check sooner. Calls and music are not forcibly restarted.
The iPhone companion and its current App Store submission are unchanged. This release updates the direct-download Mac app only.
## Validation
287 regression tests (5 skipped, no failures), seven focused audio-access tests, DSP sanitizer checks, light/dark recovery views, Apple Silicon and Intel builds, plus live Spotify/reconnect checks on the development Mac. Missing/obsolete approvals are covered with synthetic silent-input tests; working Mac permissions were not revoked to simulate failure.
